semantic_findings: The single recorded writer of the slot, 0x00d3b9b0, is a constructor-shaped body: it writes four vtable-ish pointers into the object (*param_1 = &PTR_FUN_0147ac70 and three more at +4/+8/+0xc), zeroes a long run of fields, then ends with App__sCreatureModeStrategy = param_1; return param_1;. Its tail reads live as 00d3baae 89 35 94 e2 69 01 MOV [0x0169e294],ESI / 8b c6 MOV EAX,ESI / 5e / 5b / c3. It publishes its own incoming object pointer, which is what makes the slot's contents an object address.

Caller 0x00d4c5e0 calls this entry twice and each time moves the result into ECX before a member call: 00d4c624 CALL 0x00d38840 / 00d4c629 MOV ECX,EAX / 00d4c62b CALL 0x00d39360, then 00d4c635 CALL 0x00d38840 / 00d4c63a MOV ECX,EAX / 00d4c63c CALL 0x00d3cdc0. 0x00d39360 decompiles with the signature App__cCreatureModeStrategy__ExecuteAction(cCreatureModeStrategy *this, uint32_t actionID, void *actionData), so ECX is that method's `this`.

Readers index through the loaded word: 0x00d395a4 does MOV EAX,[0x0169e294] then DEC/INC dword ptr [EAX+0x24]; 0x00d2b6e0 writes a byte at +0xdc; 0x00d2c280 loads a dword at +0xb4. These are recorded as facts about THOSE functions' reach and are explicitly not used to size or type anything in this package.

0x00d395a4 is a sibling that loads the same absolute address INLINE rather than calling this entry - the same read spelled differently, and the reason this accessor has callers that also read the slot themselves.

Pinned sidecars agree on shape: knowledgegraph/triage/xrefs-2540f2ca.tsv records 59 direct-call edges in from 39 distinct callers, 0 edges out, and no other reference type. knowledgegraph/triage/datarefs-2540f2ca.tsv records exactly one row with 0x00d38840 as referencer (the read of 0x0169e294 at callsite 0x00d38840, access mode read, segment .data -wr) and zero rows with 0x00d38840 as target. For the slot itself: 47 read rows and exactly ONE write row, at 0x00d3baae. The single-writer claim is therefore measured, not assumed.
summary: FUN_00d38840 is a six-byte global-instance accessor: `MOV EAX,[0x0169e294]; RET`. Opcode 0xa1 is MOV r32,moffs32, an absolute form with no ModRM byte and no base register, so there is no receiver and no displacement/index hazard. The address 0x0169e294 is the Ghidra-labelled global `App::sCreatureModeStrategy` in .data. The return is declared void* on writer-and-caller evidence, not on the derived record's pointer_like heuristic: the only recorded writer (0x00d3b9b0) is a constructor-shaped body that stores its own incoming object pointer into the slot at 0x00d3baae and returns it, and callers use the result as a receiver (0x00d4c5e0 twice, MOV ECX,EAX before a member call) or index through it at 0x24/0xdc/0xb4. The pointee's CLASS is deliberately not claimed: the slot's label reads App::sCreatureModeStrategy while the callee names a TYPE App::cCreatureModeStrategy, and the binary has no MSVC RTTI to tie them together. No calling convention is asserted because the body is byte-identical under all four candidates. No runtime claim: the axis is GATED and unattempted.

unresolved_questions: What TYPE the slot's pointee is. The evidence establishes that it is an object pointer - one writer publishes `this`, and callers use the result as a receiver and index through it - but not its class. The slot's Ghidra label is App::sCreatureModeStrategy while the callee names a TYPE App::cCreatureModeStrategy, and this binary has no MSVC RTTI, so nothing machine-derived ties the two together. Promoting cCreatureModeStrategy to the C type needs RTTI, a vtable-shape match, or an SDK-proven static-member declaration.
Whether 0x00d3b9b0 is the ONLY writer across the whole program. The pinned sidecar and the live database each record one write row for the slot; neither covers unanalysed or dynamically-reached code.
Whether the slot is ever null in the running process, and therefore whether any caller has a latent null dereference. The runtime axis is GATED and unattempted, so nothing here answers it.

Whether all 39 recorded callers use the result the same way. Four were sampled (0x00d4c5e0, 0x00d395a4, 0x00d2b6e0, 0x00d2c280); the other 35 were not, so 'every caller treats it as a receiver' is not claimed.
Whether the absolute slot address can ever be modelled as a real dereference rather than a stood-up object. That needs the original image mapped, which is outside what this package does.
